_doc: Where locals actually look things up, per country. Templates take {q} (URL-encoded query) and optionally {city} (from the platform's cities map, keyed by the spot's region/destination names; no match means no link). verified = what tools/check_links.py measured: 'ok' (search page returned results to a plain HTTP client), 'challenge' (bot wall, format from the platform's own UI, works in a real browser), 'login' (needs the user signed in). query = 'local' uses the local-script name when we have one.
_countries_doc: dine = Dine, Markets and Cafes cards; any = every other category. First entry is the primary button. why = one line shown in the app's Local sources sheet.

SG.why: Burpple and Eatbook are Singapore-only review sites; Google Maps reviews and TikTok drive most queues.

MY.why: Google Maps reviews dominate; Xiaohongshu is heavily used by Malaysian Chinese, TikTok by everyone.

TH.why: Wongnai (merged with LINE MAN) is Thailand's own restaurant review platform.

VN.why: Foody.vn (ShopeeFood's review side) is Vietnam's local food review site, searched per city.

ID.why: No local review site survived; Indonesians use Google Maps reviews, TikTok and Instagram.

PH.why: Zomato left in 2020; Google Maps, TikTok and Facebook food groups carry local word of mouth.

KH.why: Facebook is effectively Cambodia's internet; most places only have a Facebook page.

LA.why: Facebook pages and Google Maps; no local review platform.

MM.why: Facebook is the default local source; Google Maps for locations.

BN.why: Small market; Instagram and Google Maps are where Bruneians post and check places.

TL.why: Facebook and Google Maps; very little else is indexed.

JP.why: Tabelog is the Japanese benchmark for food; Retty is the second review site.

KR.why: Koreans use Naver Map and Kakao Map; Google Maps is weak in Korea by law.

CN.why: Dianping for food, Xiaohongshu for discovery, Amap or Baidu for maps; Google is blocked.

TW.why: Taiwan runs on Google Maps reviews; iFoodie and Dcard are local but not linkable by search.

HK.why: OpenRice is Hong Kong's restaurant review standard.

MO.why: OpenRice covers Macau as well as Hong Kong.
